course: Daily Bread Sales: Bakery Production System

lessons.title: Introduction and Why It Matters
lessons.body: Food safety is not just a legal requirementâit is the foundation of your bakery business. In many African countries, customers buy bread daily, and a single case of food poisoning can destroy your reputation overnight. You must understand that harmful bacteria like Salmonella and E. coli can grow rapidly in dough, fillings, and on surfaces if you are not careful. For example, if you sell bread that makes a family sick, word will spread fast in your community, and you could lose all your customers. Moreover, without proper licensing, health inspectors can shut you down and fine you. Licensing shows customers and authorities that you meet basic hygiene standards. In Kenya, for instance, you need a food handler's certificate and a county health license. In Nigeria, you need to register with NAFDAC and get a food safety permit. These cost money and time, but they protect your business. Imagine selling 100 loaves a day at 50 cents eachâthatâs $50 daily. If you get shut down for a week, you lose $350. Thatâs why investing in safety and licensing is smart. Also, safe food lasts longer, so you waste less. Simple practices like washing hands, cleaning surfaces, and storing ingredients properly reduce spoilage. In this module, you will learn the tools, methods, and steps to keep your bakery safe and legally compliant. We will cover how to clean, how to handle food, how to avoid common mistakes, and how to get licensed. By the end, you will be able to run a bakery that customers trust and inspectors approve.

lessons.title: Tools and Materials
lessons.body: To run a safe bakery, you need specific tools and materials. First, for cleaning: you need at least two bucketsâone for soapy water and one for rinse water. Use a food-safe detergent, not ordinary laundry soap. A stiff-bristled brush for scrubbing floors and a soft brush for equipment. You also need clean cloths or disposable paper towels. For personal hygiene: soap, clean water, and a nail brush. A handwashing station with a tap or a jerrycan with a spigot is essential. If you donât have running water, use a tippy-tapâa jerrycan hung with a string to tip and release water. You also need sanitizer, like bleach diluted in water (1 tablespoon per gallon) or commercial food-safe sanitizer. For storage: airtight containers for flour, sugar, and yeast. Label them with dates. A thermometer to check fridge and freezer temperatures (fridge should be below 5Â°C, freezer below -18Â°C). For pest control: traps, screens on windows, and sealed bins. For licensing: a folder to keep certificates, receipts, and inspection reports. You will also need a food handler's certificate for each worker, which requires a medical test. In many African cities, you can get this at a local clinic for about $10-$20. Finally, keep a first aid kit and fire extinguisher. All these tools are affordable and can be sourced locally. For example, in Ghana, you can buy food-grade buckets at Makola Market. In South Africa, check hardware stores like Builders Warehouse. Investing in these tools costs less than a single fine or lost business.

lessons.title: Step by Step Method
lessons.body: Follow these steps daily to ensure food safety and maintain your license. Step 1: Personal hygiene. Before starting, wash hands with soap and warm water for 20 seconds. Dry with a clean towel. Wear clean apron, hairnet, and if you have a cold, a mask. Step 2: Clean and sanitize surfaces. Remove all crumbs and debris. Wash with hot soapy water, then rinse. Spray or wipe with sanitizer. Let air dry. Do this before and after each use. Step 3: Handle ingredients safely. Check expiry dates. Store flour in airtight containers off the floor. Keep eggs refrigerated. Wash fruits and vegetables. Step 4: Control temperature. When baking, ensure internal temperature of bread reaches at least 90Â°C to kill bacteria. Cool bread on racks, not on the floor. Store finished bread in clean, covered containers. Step 5: Clean equipment. After use, disassemble mixers, bowls, and trays. Wash with hot soapy water, rinse, sanitize, and air dry. Step 6: Manage waste. Put trash in covered bins. Remove daily. Step 7: Pest control. Check for signs of rats, cockroaches, or flies. Set traps and seal entry points. Step 8: Record keeping. Keep a log of cleaning times, temperatures, and any issues. Step 9: Licensing. Apply for health permit at your local council. Submit required documents: ID, medical certificates for staff, floor plan, and fee. Inspectors will visit. If you pass, you get a license. Renew annually. Step 10: Train staff. Hold short weekly meetings on hygiene. By following these steps, you protect your customers and your business.

lessons.title: Common Mistakes and Fixes
lessons.body: Many bakeries fail inspections or cause illness due to common mistakes. Here are the top ones and how to fix them. Mistake 1: Not washing hands often. Fix: Wash before handling food, after using toilet, after touching money, and after handling raw eggs. Keep a handwashing station nearby. Mistake 2: Using dirty cloths. Fix: Use disposable paper towels or change cloths daily and wash them in hot water. Mistake 3: Cross-contamination. Using the same board for raw dough and ready-to-eat bread. Fix: Use color-coded cutting boardsâred for raw, green for ready-to-eat. Mistake 4: Improper storage. Leaving flour open, attracting pests. Fix: Store in airtight containers, label with date, and use oldest first. Mistake 5: Ignoring temperatures. Not checking fridge or freezer. Fix: Keep a thermometer in each unit and check twice daily. Record readings. Mistake 6: Poor pest control. Seeing droppings but doing nothing. Fix: Act immediatelyâset traps, seal cracks, and call a pest control service if needed. Mistake 7: No license. Operating without a permit. Fix: Visit your local health office, ask for requirements, and start the process. It may take a few weeks, but itâs worth it. Mistake 8: Not training staff. Assuming everyone knows. Fix: Conduct monthly training on hygiene and safety. Mistake 9: Using expired ingredients. Fix: Check dates weekly and rotate stock. Mistake 10: Ignoring customer complaints. Fix: Take any illness complaint seriously, investigate, and correct. By avoiding these mistakes, you build trust and avoid fines.

lessons.title: Safety and Best Practice
lessons.body: Safety goes beyond cleaningâitâs a mindset. Best practices include: Always wear clean uniform and closed shoes. Tie back hair. Donât wear jewelry that can fall into dough. If you have cuts, cover with waterproof bandage and glove. Never smoke or eat in the bakery. Store chemicals away from food. Use food-safe sanitizers only. Keep floors dry to prevent slips. Ensure good ventilation. Use fire extinguisher and know how to use it. For licensing, keep records of all training, cleaning, and inspections. Display your license where customers can see it. This builds confidence. In many African countries, health inspectors look for specific things: handwashing facilities, clean toilets, proper waste disposal, and pest control. They also check that staff have food handler certificates. To get certified, you and your staff must take a short course and medical test. In Kenya, itâs called a Food Handlerâs Certificate, issued by the Ministry of Health. In Nigeria, you need a Food Safety Certificate from NAFDAC. In South Africa, a Certificate of Acceptability from the municipality. Costs vary: $20-$100. Renew annually. Also, consider liability insurance if available. Best practice includes regular self-inspection. Create a checklist and go through it weekly. Involve your team. Reward good hygiene. Remember, safe food is good business. Customers will return if they trust your bread. And you avoid legal troubles. So make safety a habit, not a one-time task.

lessons.title: Practical Exercise
lessons.body: Now itâs time to put what you learned into action. This exercise will help you set up a food safety and licensing plan for your bakery. Follow these steps: 1. Conduct a self-inspection. Walk through your bakery and list all areas that need improvement. Use a checklist: handwashing station, cleaning supplies, storage, pest control, and records. 2. Create a cleaning schedule. For each day of the week, assign tasks: e.g., Monday: clean mixer, Tuesday: clean floors, etc. Post it on the wall. 3. Set up a handwashing station. If you donât have one, build a tippy-tap using a jerrycan, rope, and soap. Place it near the entrance. 4. Train your staff. Hold a 30-minute session on handwashing and cross-contamination. Use the steps from Lesson 3. 5. Gather licensing documents. Visit your local health office and ask for requirements. Typically, you need: ID copies, medical certificates for staff, floor plan, and application fee. Start the process. 6. Create a record book. Log daily cleaning, fridge temperatures, and any pest sightings. 7. Practice a mock inspection. Ask a friend to act as an inspector and check your bakery. Fix any issues. 8. Calculate costs. List expenses for cleaning supplies, certificates, and fees. Compare with potential fines (e.g., $100) and lost business. 9. Set a goal. Aim to get licensed within 3 months. Break it into weekly tasks. 10. Review and improve. After one month, check whatâs working and whatâs not. Adjust. By completing this exercise, you will have a safer bakery and be on your way to full licensing. Remember, this is an investment in your future.

quiz.q: Why is food safety important for a bakery business?
options: A) It increases the price of bread
B) It prevents customers from getting sick and builds trust
C) It allows you to use cheaper ingredients
D) It is only needed for large bakeries
quiz.explanation: Food safety prevents illness and builds customer trust, which is essential for repeat business.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a key reason to get a food license?
options: B) To sell bread at a higher price
C) To legally operate and avoid fines or shutdown
quiz.explanation: A license allows you to operate legally and protects you from fines or closure by health inspectors.

quiz.q: What is a food handler's certificate?
options: A) A document proving you own the bakery
B) A certificate showing you have been trained in food safety
C) A receipt for buying baking equipment
D) A license to sell bread in multiple countries
quiz.explanation: A food handler's certificate is issued after training and a medical test, proving you handle food safely.

quiz.q: In Kenya, which authority issues food handler's certificates?
quiz.explanation: In Kenya, the Ministry of Health issues food handler's certificates after training and medical tests.

quiz.q: What is a tippy-tap used for?
options: B) Handwashing when there is no running water
quiz.explanation: A tippy-tap is a simple handwashing station made from a jerrycan, used when there is no running water.

quiz.q: Which of these is a food-safe sanitizer?
quiz.explanation: Diluted bleach (1 tablespoon per gallon) is a common food-safe sanitizer for surfaces.

quiz.q: What is the correct temperature for a refrigerator?
quiz.explanation: A refrigerator should be kept below 5Â°C to slow bacterial growth.

quiz.q: Why should you use color-coded cutting boards?
options: B) To prevent cross-contamination between raw and ready-to-eat foods
quiz.explanation: Color-coded boards help prevent cross-contamination by separating raw and ready-to-eat foods.

quiz.q: What should you do if you have a cut on your hand while baking?
options: B) Cover with a waterproof bandage and wear a glove
C) Wash it with soap and continue without covering
D) Stop baking for the day
quiz.explanation: Covering a cut with a waterproof bandage and glove prevents infection from spreading to food.

quiz.q: How often should you clean and sanitize work surfaces?
options: C) Before and after each use
quiz.explanation: Cleaning and sanitizing before and after each use prevents bacterial buildup.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake that leads to food poisoning?
options: C) Not washing hands after using the toilet
D) Storing food in airtight containers
quiz.explanation: Not washing hands after using the toilet can transfer harmful bacteria to food.

quiz.q: How should you store flour to prevent pests?
options: A) In an open bag on the floor
B) In an airtight container off the floor
quiz.explanation: Airtight containers off the floor prevent pests and moisture from contaminating flour.

quiz.q: What is the correct way to cool bread?
options: C) In a closed container while hot
D) Stacked on top of each other
quiz.explanation: Cooling on a clean rack allows air circulation and prevents condensation and bacterial growth.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep a record book in the bakery?
options: B) To record cleaning, temperatures, and issues for inspection
quiz.explanation: Records help you monitor safety practices and show inspectors you are compliant.

quiz.q: What should you do if you see cockroaches in the bakery?
options: B) Set traps and seal entry points immediately
C) Spray with insecticide near food
D) Close the bakery for a week
quiz.explanation: Immediate action with traps and sealing cracks prevents infestation and contamination.

quiz.q: What is the first step in personal hygiene before baking?
options: B) Wash hands with soap and water for 20 seconds
quiz.explanation: Washing hands for 20 seconds is the first step to prevent contamination.

quiz.q: Which of these is a best practice for safe food handling?
options: C) Wearing a clean apron and hairnet
quiz.explanation: Wearing clean apron and hairnet prevents hair and dirt from contaminating food.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a food safety license?
options: B) To show customers you meet health standards
D) To allow you to sell anywhere
quiz.explanation: A license demonstrates to customers and authorities that you meet health standards.

quiz.q: How often should you renew your food license?
quiz.explanation: Food licenses typically need to be renewed annually.

quiz.q: What should you do with expired ingredients?
options: C) Sell them at a discount
quiz.explanation: Expired ingredients can be unsafe and should be discarded.

quiz.q: What is a self-inspection?
options: A) An inspection by the health department
B) A check you do yourself to find and fix safety issues
quiz.explanation: Self-inspection is when you regularly check your own bakery for safety and hygiene issues.

quiz.q: Why is training staff important for food safety?
options: B) It ensures everyone follows safe practices
C) It reduces the number of staff needed
D) It is required by law only for large bakeries
quiz.explanation: Training ensures all staff know and follow correct hygiene and safety procedures.

quiz.q: What should you do if a customer complains about illness after eating your bread?
options: C) Investigate and correct the issue
quiz.explanation: Taking complaints seriously and investigating helps prevent future incidents and builds trust.

quiz.q: Which of these is a pest control measure?
options: B) Sealing cracks and using traps
D) Storing garbage inside the bakery
quiz.explanation: Sealing cracks and using traps are effective pest control measures.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep floors dry?
options: A) To prevent slips and falls
B) To make the bakery look clean
quiz.explanation: Dry floors prevent accidents and injuries from slipping.

quiz.q: What is the correct dilution for bleach sanitizer?
options: A) 1 tablespoon per gallon of water
B) 1 cup per gallon of water
C) 1 liter per gallon of water
quiz.explanation: 1 tablespoon of bleach per gallon of water is a safe and effective sanitizing solution.

quiz.q: What should you wear to cover your hair while baking?
options: B) A hairnet or clean scarf
quiz.explanation: A hairnet or clean scarf prevents hair from falling into food.

quiz.q: What is the minimum internal temperature for baked bread to ensure safety?
quiz.explanation: Bread should reach at least 90Â°C internally to kill harmful bacteria.

quiz.q: Which document is typically required for a food license application?
options: A) A copy of your ID
quiz.explanation: A copy of your ID is usually required for identification when applying for a food license.

quiz.q: What is the benefit of displaying your food license?
options: B) It shows you are legally compliant and builds trust
C) It allows you to charge higher prices
D) It is required by law only for restaurants
quiz.explanation: Displaying your license shows customers you meet health standards and are legally operating.
